title: Let users know if one of their destinations is also in use by another user
body:
### Is your proposal related to a problem?

With allowing multiple phone numbers and email addresses per person, there is the danger that one user can spam another user by setting the other user's phone number/email address as the first user's destination.

If we make a specific phone-number/email address unique for the entire system then a user can "steal" a specific phone number/email address from another user and prevent its usage by that other user.

### Desired solution

By allowing a user to see if a phone number/email address is already in use (and by whom) the users themselves have the opportunity to work out which destinations should receive what.
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
I don't think it's a good idea to inform users which other users are using a destination address. I would consider that a breach of privacy.

It might be okay to tell a user that "some other user is already using this destination address", but that should still not prevent a user from doing so.

Also, I would consider this a very low priority issue.

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
> It might be okay to tell a user that "some other user is already using this destination address", but that should still not prevent a user from doing so.

Although, this could still be a breach of privacy. If you want to know if John Doe is a user of the system, and you know their e-mail is john.doe@example.org, you could attempt to add that address and be told in clear text that "yes, John Doe probably has an account here" (of course, this scenario could be a bit far fetched in an enterprise setting anyway).

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body: I agree with @lunkwill42. It is sufficient for a user to know whether a destination already exists or not. If they do get spam they can ask an admin to figure out who else uses that destination. IIRC per user, a destination should only exist once anyway but how to tell a user that they've already made that specific destination is out of scope for this issue.

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body:
Notes from in person discussion:
An endpoint should be added that given a primary key for an existing destination finds out if there exists a different destination with the same medium and the same settings and simply returns a boolean
